title: Optimize INT8/FP8 quantized kernels: fused dequant + smoothquant paths, KV-cache-aware scheduling and continuous batching
author: Aisha Khan
body:
Context: Customers and internal benchmarks show that INT8/FP8 quantized inference is a key lever for lowering unit cost. However, we observed excess overheads in the runtime when switching between dequantized and quantized execution paths, duplicated memory copies during smoothquant scaling, and suboptimal batching/scheduling interactions with the KV cache for long-chat workloads. This PR implements a set of complementary changes to reduce per-token overhead and improve end-to-end throughput/latency for quantized models.

Summary of changes:
1) Kernel-level fusion: implement fused dequantize->smoothquant->GEMM path for INT8/FP8 where model metadata indicates smoothquant scaling factors are present. This reduces intermediate allocations and memory traffic and enables a single-pass requantization/accumulate step.
2) Requantization micro-optimizations: new fast-path for per-channel requantization using AVX512/AMX-friendly loop ordering and precomputed scale tables for common per-tensor cases.
3) KV-cache-aware scheduler: continuous-batching scheduler updated to respect KV cache locality for chat-like workloads (preserve hot-key segmentation, prefer batching queries that share KV addresses). Adds heuristics to avoid oversized batches that cause KV cache thrashing.
4) Batching/coalescing: improve continuous batching logic to coalesce requests with compatible sequence length and quantization profiles to maximize vectorized GEMM efficiency.
5) Unit tests, integration tests, and perf harness updates: new microbenchmarks for fused path, end-to-end canary on perf-canary cluster, and CI tests ensuring numeric parity within tolerance.

Motivation: The runtime previously paid a ~5-10us penalty per layer for switching between quantized and dequantized paths and copying smoothquant scale factors per-token. By fusing operations and aligning memory/layout assumptions with the GEMM kernels, we reduce that overhead and increase throughput on typical LLM workloads (seq128-seq512).

Design notes:
- The fused path is guarded behind model metadata flags and a runtime capability check; we fall back to the safe dequant->gemm->requant flow when unsupported.
- Numeric safety: we run a tight set of determinism checks and tolerance-based equality tests against the FP16 baseline. The PR includes per-layer accumulation checks and a regression test harness to detect >0.5 L2 norm deviation per layer.
- Scheduler changes are additive and configurable via runtime flags: kvcache.batch_locality=true by default for dedicated and hosted runtimes.
- Rollout plan: canary on perf-canary (10%), then progressive rollout to dedicated, then hosted after 48h with no regressions.

Changes included (high-level):
- src/runtime/kernels/quant_fused_gemm.cc
- src/runtime/kernels/quant_requant_fastpath.cc
- src/runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cc
- src/runtime/scheduler/kvcache_locality_policy.cc
- tests/quant/fused_path_microbench.cc
- perf/canary/configs/quant_fusion_canary.yaml
- docs/ops/quantization.md (implementation notes + rollout guide)

Testing and results: Microbenchmarks (x86 AVX512, A100 equivalent runs on perf-canary):
- INT8 fused path (seq128): throughput +1.45x, p95 latency -14%
- FP8 fused path (seq128): throughput +1.30x, p95 latency -10%
- End-to-end chat workload (seq512, batch dynamic): throughput +1.22x, 99th latency -12%

Regression: numeric diffs within tolerance for 98.7% of evaluated layers; flagged layers have a separate guardrail enabling fallback.

CI: initial run surfaced a flaky kernel alignment test; fix included in second commit and CI passed.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel fusion implementation
- [x] Scheduler and batching heuristics
- [x] Tests and perf canary
- [x] Docs and ops runbook
- [x] Feature-flag gating and safe fallback

Related tickets: Linear: ENG-2045, ENG-3071, ENG-4410. This PR is performance-focused and non-breaking; behavior preserved via runtime guards.

release_notes: Performance: Fused INT8/FP8 quantized GEMM path and KV-cache-aware batching; throughput improvements up to ~1.45x on INT8 workloads and reduced tail latency. Non-breaking, guarded by runtime flags.
benchmark_summary: Microbench kernel perf: reduced per-layer overhead by ~6-11us depending on sequence length

Hosted: progressive rollout dependent on canary health and perf signals
